sections.title: Executive Summary + Investment Thesis
sections.body:
**Executive Summary + Investment Thesis**

Bharti Airtel (BHARTIARTL) has demonstrated a significant improvement in its cash flows from operating activities, with a net cash generation of ₹983,322 million in the year ended March 31, 2025, as per the consolidated statement of cash flows. This represents a notable increase from ₹788,982 million in the previous year. The company's profit before tax has also shown a substantial rise to ₹383,985 million in the year ended March 31, 2025, from ₹126,790 million in the previous year. 

Our investment thesis is centered around BHARTIARTL's ability to sustain its operating cash flow growth, driven by its robust profit before tax and effective management of working capital. Although the company's cash outflows from investing and financing activities remain significant, primarily due to payments towards spectrum acquisitions and debt repayments, we believe that its strong operating cash flows will enable it to navigate these challenges. With a net increase in cash and cash equivalents of ₹15,292 million during the year, the company's liquidity position appears stable. However, the absence of net worth and net profit (PAT) data in the provided excerpts limits our ability to conduct a comprehensive analysis of the company's financial performance. Nonetheless, based on the available data, we remain cautiously optimistic about BHARTIARTL's prospects, driven by its improving cash flow profile and profit growth.

sections.title: Business Overview + Segment Breakdown
sections.body:
Bharti Airtel Limited operates across multiple business segments, including Mobile Services India, Mobile Services Africa, Mobile Services South Asia, Airtel Business, Passive Infrastructure Services, Homes Services, Digital TV Services, and Others. The company's segments are evaluated based on segment revenue and segment result, which includes profit or loss from operating activities before exceptional items and tax. As per the latest available information, the company has reported a profit after tax of ₹235,018 million and revenue of ₹1,089,439 million. The company's business segments cater to a wide range of customers, including individual consumers and large corporations, providing services such as voice and data telecom services, digital solutions, and passive infrastructure services.

The company's segment breakdown includes Mobile Services India, which provides voice and data telecom services through wireless technology in India, Mobile Services Africa, which provides similar services in Africa, and Airtel Business, which provides end-to-end telecom solutions to large corporations. The company also operates in the digital TV services space, providing digital broadcasting services under the DTH platform and IPTV services. The Homes Services segment provides voice and data communications through fixed-line network, wireless network, and broadband technology for homes. The company's Manufactured Capital includes 338,029 mobile network towers, 992,465 mobile broadband base stations, and 7.2 million fiber home passes rolled out in FY 2024-25. The company has spent ₹68.6 billion on acquiring spectrum in FY 2024-25, indicating its focus on expanding its network capabilities. However, specific segment-wise revenue and profitability details are not available in the provided excerpts.

sections.title: Financial Performance
sections.body:
The financial performance of Bharti Airtel (BHARTIARTL) is reflected in its consolidated and standalone cash flow statements for the years ended March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024. On a consolidated basis, the company's profit before tax increased significantly to ₹38,398.5 crore in FY2025 from ₹12,679 crore in FY2024. The consolidated net cash generated from operating activities stood at ₹98,332.2 crore in FY2025, up from ₹78,898.2 crore in the previous year. The company's investing activities resulted in a net outflow of ₹60,269.8 crore in FY2025, primarily due to payments towards spectrum acquisitions and purchase of property, plant, and equipment.

On a standalone basis, the company's profit before tax increased to ₹17,864.4 crore in FY2025 from ₹7,116.1 crore in FY2024. The standalone net cash generated from operating activities was ₹62,336.3 crore in FY2025, compared to ₹53,208.8 crore in the previous year. The company's investing activities on a standalone basis resulted in a net outflow of ₹41,452.9 crore in FY2025, primarily due to payments towards spectrum acquisitions and purchase of property, plant, and equipment. However, the filing excerpts do not provide information on the company's net profit (PAT) or net worth (shareholders' equity), which are essential metrics for a comprehensive analysis of its financial performance.

sections.title: Balance Sheet Health + Cash Flow
sections.body:
The balance sheet health and cash flow of Bharti Airtel (BHARTIARTL) can be assessed through its consolidated and standalone statements of cash flows. For the year ended March 31, 2025, the company's consolidated net cash generated from operating activities stood at ₹983,322 million, a significant increase from ₹788,982 million in the previous year. This was driven by a substantial rise in profit before tax, which was ₹383,985 million for the year ended March 31, 2025, compared to ₹126,790 million for the year ended March 31, 2024. The company's consolidated cash flows from investing activities resulted in a net outflow of ₹602,698 million, primarily due to payments towards spectrum acquisitions and purchases of property, plant, and equipment.

The company's standalone statement of cash flows also reflects a similar trend, with net cash generated from operating activities increasing to ₹623,363 million for the year ended March 31, 2025, from ₹532,088 million in the previous year. The standalone cash flows from investing activities resulted in a net outflow of ₹414,529 million, primarily due to payments towards spectrum acquisitions and purchases of property, plant, and equipment. The company's cash and cash equivalents as at the end of the year stood at ₹6,628 million, indicating a moderate increase from the beginning of the year. However, the information provided does not include the company's net worth or detailed balance sheet data, limiting a comprehensive assessment of its balance sheet health.

sections.title: Recent Developments
sections.body:
Recent Developments
The company has adopted new accounting standards and amendments during the year, including Ind AS 117 relating to the accounting of Insurance Contracts and amendments to Ind AS 116 relating to the accounting for sale and leaseback transactions with variable lease payments, effective April 1, 2024. Additionally, the Group has changed the classification of distribution costs relating to its Africa mobile money business, reclassifying these costs from other operating expenses to sales and marketing expenses in the Statement of Profit and Loss. The company has also spent ₹68.6 billion on acquiring spectrum in FY 2024-25 and rolled out 7.2 million fiber home passes. Furthermore, the company has achieved a landmark year of value-creation, marked by a lifetime high market share, highest-ever revenues of ₹1,089,439 million, and sustained operational excellence, with a net debt to EBITDAaL ratio of 2.1x. 

The company's recent financial performance includes revenue of ₹1,089,439 million, EBITDAaL margin of 49%, and profit after tax of ₹235,018 million. The company has also generated ₹585,388 million in cash from operations and paid ₹533,745 million to the exchequer. The company's net worth, as represented by its equity, stands at ₹1,401,311 million, and its net debt is ₹1,608,221 million.

sections.title: Bull vs Bear vs Base Case
sections.body:
The bull case for Bharti Airtel Limited (BHARTIARTL) is supported by the company's strong revenue growth, with a 15.8% year-over-year (Y-o-Y) increase in revenue from ₹941,198 million in FY 2023-24 to ₹1,089,439 million in FY 2024-25. Additionally, the company's focus on operational efficiency and digital acceleration is expected to drive long-term growth. The achievement of an industry-leading average revenue per user (ARPU) of ₹245, representing a Y-o-Y increase of ₹36, further bolsters the bull case. 

In contrast, the bear case highlights potential challenges, including the company's exposure to regulatory risks and intense competition in the Indian telecom market. However, specific details on these risks are not provided in the context. The base case scenario is supported by the company's strategic pillars, including prudent capital allocation, operational excellence, and digital acceleration, which are expected to drive sustained financial performance. With a net debt to EBITDAaL ratio of 2.1x and an EBITDAaL margin of 49.0%, the company's financial position appears stable, supporting the base case scenario.

Strong cash generation supports balance sheet deleveraging and a step-up in dividends. We continue to channelise investments into strengthening and expanding our digital network to enhance customer experience and foster long-term relationships with them. This approach enables us to create enduring value for our stakeholders. We added 9 million mobile customers and 24 million smartphone data customers. This helped us achieve industry leading growth, translating to lifetime high revenue market share. Attracting and retaining high-value customers remains the cornerstone of our strategy. We have achieved an industry-leading ARPU of C245, a Y-o-Y increase of C36. Segment’s performance is evaluated based on segment revenue and segment result viz. profit or loss from operating activities before exceptional items and tax, after excluding charity and donation cost but including share of result of joint ventures and associates. Accordingly, finance costs / income, non-operating (income) / expenses and exceptional items are not allocated to individual segment. Inter-segment pricing and terms are reviewed and changed by the management to reflect changes in market conditions and changes to such terms are reflected in the period in which the changes occur. Inter-segment revenues are eliminated upon consolidation of segments / Group accounting policy alignments are reflected in the ‘Eliminations / Adjustments’ column. Segment assets / liabilities comprise assets / liabilities directly managed by each segment. Segment assets primarily includes receivables, ROU, PPE, CWIP, intangible assets, IAUD, non-current investments, inventories and cash and cash equivalents. Segment liabilities primarily include operating and lease liabilities. Segment capital expenditure comprises of additions to PPE, CWIP, intangible assets, and IAUD, ROU and capital advances. The reporting segments of the Group are as below: Mobile Services India: These services cover voice and data telecom services provided through wireless technology (2G / 4G / 5G) in India. This includes the captive national long distance networks which primarily provide connectivity to the mobile services business in India. This also includes intra-city fibre networks. Mobile Services Africa: These services cover provision of voice and data telecom services provided through wireless technology (2G / 3G / 4G) and mobile money services in Africa. This also includes corporate headquarter costs of the Group’s Africa operations. Mobile Services South Asia: These services cover voice and data telecom services provided through wireless technology (2G / 3G / 4G) in Sri Lanka. Airtel Business: These services cover end-to-end telecom solutions being provided to large Indian and global corporations by serving as a single point of contact for all telecommunication needs across data and voice (domestic as well as international long distance), network integration and managed services. It also includes digital solutions such as cloud, security and platform services. Passive Infrastructure Services: These services include setting up, operating and maintaining wireless communication towers in India. Homes Services: These services cover voice and data communications through fixed-line network, wireless network and broadband technology for homes. Digital TV Services: This includes digital broadcasting services provided under the DTH platform and IPTV services. Others: It includes certain other strategic investment in joint venture / associates, and administrative / support services provided to other segments. Unallocated: It includes expenses / results, assets and liabilities primarily of corporate headquarters of the Group, non-current investment, current taxes, deferred taxes, borrowings and certain financial assets and liabilities, not allocated to the operating segments. eval_context.content: a tricky monetary policy trajectory based on varying inflation trends. Growth has shown diverging trends across the region, with larger economies showing improving economic fundamentals but emerging economies still heavily dependent on natural resources and external factors. Countries like Nigeria and Angola benefitted from the boom in oil production while metal-exporting countries like Zambia faced downward pressure from a fall in metal prices. The region will have to overcome the challenge of rising food insecurity and depreciating currencies to tackle inflation and boost growth. Countries like Nigeria have led the way through effective macroeconomic and fiscal reforms, including a tighter monetary policy and improved revenue administration. Outlook According to the World Bank, growth in the region will likely rise to 4.1% in 2025. Most economies in Sub-Saharan Africa should regain momentum as easing inflation lifts private consumption and investment, while resource-rich countries will profit from rising exports. However, progress will depend on how well the region navigates shifting trade policies and geopolitical tensions. The recent rise in protectionist measures and tariffs, globally and within Africa, is increasing input costs and making cross-border supply chains more complex and costly. These could reinforce the food price volatility triggered by conflict in the Middle East. An accommodative monetary stance, careful debt management and a supportive global backdrop will be essential for sustaining growth.
